text.p: These are the major headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- CAW told to vote on pay cut: Transport Minister takes unprecedented step in bid to save Canadian Airlines.
- Elderly women at risk: report says 40 percent over age 75 below poverty line.
- UN chief gives in to U.S. pressure: Boutros-Ghali drops candidacy.
- Ontario studies more contracting out: Union protections could be in jeopardy.
- N.S. to revise abuse package: Lawyers for victims expect cash to be cut as claims climb.
- Burundi caught in chaos: Buyoya regime's distain for democracy makes the Central African country the most likely spot for next eruption of Tutsi-Hutu violence.
- Royal sets profit record: Canada's biggest bank earns $1.43-billion, more than any firm in country's history.
- Hard-nosed Hargrove put to the test.
- Bre-X's fate unclear as deadline passes: Suharto may have last word on Busang as company, Barrick fail to finalize deal.
- Suncor plans $250-million pipeline: Wants to bolster oil sands group.
- CAW vows to fight forced vote on wage-cut plan: Canadian Airlines CEO Kevin Benson gets reprieve as Labor Minister Alfonso Gagliano orders union to put restructuring plan to its 3,700 members.
- Bre-X still driving for better Busang deal.
